title: Slot fencing and pressure-policy tuning for micro-batch admission under sustained high QPS
creator: Aisha Ramesh
description:
Summary: We observe recurring SLA violations during sustained high QPS bursts on c5-like workloads where we see KV cache growth combined with bursty microbatch arrivals. Current admission logic uses a simple headroom threshold and token-slot accounting which underestimates transient KV pressure from repeated long-prefix requests. This ticket implements a slot-fencing admission policy + pressure-policy tuning to make micro-batch acceptance decisions robust to sustained high QPS while minimizing latency impact for latency-sensitive routes.

Problem statement: Under high sustained QPS (> 12k rps in e2e tests) the KV cache expands due to many unique prefixes and the GPU memory reserved for KV and attention buffers becomes fragmented. Because the admission controller only checks instantaneous free slots and a conservative single-value KV budget, we either: (a) over-reject (increasing cold latency and tail), or (b) accept too many batches and cause OOM/evictions leading to long tail latencies and retries. Existing heuristics do not account for prefix locality, short-term KV growth rate, or per-gpu slot fencing for staged spill.

Proposed solution: 1) Slot fencing: partition GPU token-slot budget into fenced pools (fast-path / steady / spillable). Each incoming request maps to a pool based on route SLA and recent prefix hotness. Fast-path pool is small and reserved for latency-critical routes; steady pool is for common traffic; spillable pool is for opportunistic acceptance that may trigger async KV eviction. 2) Pressure policy tuning: replace single-headroom scalar with a 3-element vector: {min_free_slots, transient_growth_budget, kv_growth_delta_window_ms}. Admission checks: available_slots >= min_free_slots + predicted_growth(transient_window) - reclaimable_from_spillable. Predicted growth uses EWMA of prefix-unique-token-rate with alpha=0.15 by default and a short window (1s). 3) Prefix-aware prefetch-trimming: before admitting a batch, estimate incremental KV footprint from the prefix by using a lightweight hotness cache in CPU memory (LRU with small samples) to avoid fetching full KV items for clearly cold prefixes. 4) Gradual degrade: when pressure is high, reject or re-route to a lower-memory model variant with automated fallback.

Implementation notes: - New admission module: slot_fence_controller. Configurable via runtime flags and Console (fast-path size as percentage, default 12%). - Add a small in-memory PrefixHotness table (per-worker, sampled, bounded) with approximate cardinality counters (HyperLogLog-lite) to estimate unique prefix churn. - Integrate with existing KV retention/eviction APIs to compute reclaimable memory from spillable pool and pending async eviction throughput (tokens/sec). - Metrics: new gauges for fenced pool sizes, predicted_growth, prefix_churn_rate, admission_reject_reason.

Acceptance criteria: - No increase in P50 for latency-critical routes (>5ms change) for steady traffic. - Tail latency (P99) improvement of >= 15% under synthetic workload that previously tripped OOM/evictions. - Reduced OOMs and KV evictions in prolonged 10-minute high-QPS tests. - Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable by route via Console.

Rollout plan: staged: 1) internal dogfood on staging cluster with synthetic high-QPS harness (2 days), 2) Canary on low-traffic customer sandbox (1 week) with telemetry, 3) Gradual enable on production for non-latency-critical routes, 4) enable fast-path for latency routes after validation.

References: Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/slot-fence-admission-controller; Perf harness: https://git.internal.redwood.com/redwood/perf/harness/slot-fence; Design doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5124
comments: 2025-02-28 - Aisha Ramesh: Created ticket after reproducing OOM in staging with 10-minute sustained 12k rps test. Attached logs and heap dumps in Confluence.

2025-03-01 - Liam O'Connor: Spike completed. Verified prefix-hotness estimator (approx HLL-lite) can approximate unique prefixes within 8% error for sampled traces. Observed that instantaneous headroom underestimates 2s growth on heavy prefix churn workloads.

2025-03-03 - Engineering review: Decided to implement 3-fork slot pools (fast/steady/spillable) vs. a sliding-window single budget. PM (Ruth Chen) prefers route-configurable fast-path sizes. UX flagged need for Console knobs.

2025-03-04 - Performance QA: Initial microbench against model-a quant-8 shows P99 down ~18% when using slot fencing + prefix estimator vs baseline with same throughput. Memory fragmentation reduced measured by contiguous free slab counts. Need more long-run tests.
2025-03-05 - Security: Security review not required for this change (no external data flows), flagged to include KMS review if we later persist prefix samples.
